findings.summary: Some item sprites fail the name test from the outline alone, in every sample: the skillet reads as a magnifier, the day-pack as an apron or smock, the key ring as a wand (2 of 3), the linen towels as two documents or two shopping bags (2 of 3), and in one sample the tote's splayed handles read as a pinafore. The captions name every item, so nothing is lost for the user. The reference has no item sprites, only scenes.

On the docs holdout home page the content column stops at about 960px under a hero that spans the full width, so the right third of every section below the hero is empty. The reference home uses the whole content width under its hero.

notes: SCOPE: confirm step, 3 samples of blog, commerce, dashboard and settings (s2, s1, 032024) plus the docs and landing holdouts (s1). Looked at desktop and mobile dark screenshots of the home, detail, cart, settings and billing pages, the state captures (checkout errors, plan dialog, search empty, keyboard focus, signup errors), the drawing crops against reference p1-i2 and the motion frames. The system is dark only, so light and dark captures are identical. Known capture gap, not penalized: the settings plan-dialog scrim ends at about 900px in the full-page capture.

MEASURED LAYOUT DEFECTS: none were measured, so there was nothing to confirm or dismiss. One by-eye check, which is a false alarm: in commerce sample 1 the sweater picture column ends about 270px above the purchase column in the full-page capture (products-merino-crew-sweater-desktop-dark.png). The spec lets the shorter column stick under the header, which a full-page capture cannot show. The other two samples stay within 160px.

UPDATE GOAL (generalization, 1.3.0): REACHED in all 3 samples. Result counts are plain captions ('Showing 11 products', 'Showing 6 of 6 posts', 'Showing 8 of 8 projects'). Block meters appear only against real maximums: uptime, the bio limit (42/160), the free-shipping threshold and the rating out of 5 on the landing holdout. Each kind of screen has its own scene: a catalogue strip, a detail banner whose sign word follows the category (BAGS, WEAR), a cart strip, an article banner and a settings banner. The dashboard chart and activity panels end level in 2 of 3 samples; the third stacks them full width, which is also level. KPI tiles are one row of four. Nothing is worse than the published version.

REGRESSION CHECK: the earlier majors (rc.2 garment outlines, rc.1 sprite size) stay fixed. Sweaters, coats and tees keep sleeves that angle out from the shoulders in all three samples (home-desktop-dark.png), and the sprite ink fills about 40-50% of its window. No new blocker or major.

HOLDOUTS: both carry the language. The docs holdout (home, installation, configuration, changelog, search, copy-code, mobile nav) has a lit-building hero, 4px windows, gold primary action, framed code blocks with a Copy button and callouts, and an empty-search vignette. The landing holdout (hero, features, pricing with a highlighted gold plan, FAQ disclosures, signup error states, footer) has typed hue bars, a framed signup form with gold focus on the first invalid field, and danger frames with '!' messages. Neither copies the reference's cabin, figure or snow. No blocker there.

SIGNATURE (4): the night hero with a moon, a lit lead building with a sign, a stepped path and a hill (blog home-desktop-dark.png vs reference p1-desktop-light.png), a banner or strip per kind of screen, the framed vignette on empty states, the checkered ground strip with three set pieces on every route, the gold marker, dithered rules under h2s and hue top bars. Motion frames show stepped movement as in the reference's p1-m frames. Each sample varies the hero's cast and layout, so the scene is a recipe and not a fixed picture.

OTHER SCORES. Fidelity (4): cream pixel type, 4px windows, hard-shadow gold commits, as in reference p1-desktop-light.png. Consistency (4): the apps share the same header, rules, cards and ground strip. Hierarchy (4): scene and h1 first, then 48px KPIs, prices and plan names. States (4): gold focus frame, danger frames, a titled dialog with Cancel and a gold Confirm, vignette on empty results, hover and focus on every control. Spacing (4) and polish (4): controls that share a row share a height, radius 0, no browser defaults visible.
Earlier minors are not re-raised: the blog hero action is an outlined button, the settings and dashboard sidebars stop above the ground strip, and the dashboard table drops three columns on mobile.
VERDICT INPUT: no blocker and no major. Two minors are listed once. The candidate passes the confirm.
